描述_EN: marking the transition from childhood to adulthood, girls began to style their hair in buns with a pair of hairpins from the age of fifteen. this is also when the earliest form of chinese writing developed, and silk use was widely distributed throughout china. although men and women wore hairpins, its original owner was probably a woman. hairpins crafted from animal bones such as cattle, pig and deer were luxury items produced by local workshops for elite use. in ancient china, such hairpins symbolised an important rite of passage for young women, indicating they were ready to marry. numerous similar hairpins have been found in the tombs of aristocratic women in anyang, the capital city of the shang dynasty (1600-1046 bc), the earliest recorded dynasty in china's history. this bone hairpin (ji), carved with the figure of a stylised bird, is one of the oldest hair ornaments in the v&a.
描述_ZN: 标志着从童年到成年的过渡，女孩从15岁起就开始用一对发簪为自己的头发做发髻。 年，这也是最早的中国文字发展的时候，丝绸的使用在中国各地广泛分布。 虽然男人和女人都戴着簪子，但它的原主人可能是个女人。 用牛、猪、鹿等动物骨骼制作的发簪是由当地工场生产的供精英使用的奢侈品。 在古代中国，这种发簪象征着年轻女性的一种重要的成年仪式，表明她们已经准备好结婚。 在中国历史上最早的王朝--商朝（公元前1600-1046年）的首都安阳的贵族妇女的墓中发现了许多类似的发簪。 这个骨质发簪（ji），雕刻着一只造型鸟的形象，是V&a中最古老的发饰之一。
